bookInfo.author: Ban Gu, Ban Biao, and Ban Zhao

title.zh: 卷三十八 高五王傳
title.en: Volume 38: The Five Sons of Emperor Gao
title.raw: 卷三十八 高五王傳 Volume 38: The five sons of Emperor Gao

sentences.zh: 高皇帝八男：呂后生孝惠帝，曹夫人生齊悼惠王肥，薄姬生孝文帝，戚夫人生趙隱王如意，趙姬生淮南厲王長，諸姬生趙幽王友、趙共王恢、燕靈王建。

translations.literal: The August Emperor Gao had eight sons: Empress Lü bore Emperor Xiaohui; Lady Cao bore Prince Daohui of Qi, Fei; Consort Bo bore Emperor Xiaowen; Lady Qi bore the Hidden Prince of Zhao, Ruyi; Lady Zhao bore the Fierce Prince of Huainan, Chang; other ladies bore Prince You of Zhao the Obscure, Prince Hui of Zhao the Joint, and Prince Jian of Yan the Numinous.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gao fathered eight sons: Empress Lü gave him Emperor Xiaohui; Lady Cao gave him Prince Daohui of Qi, Liu Fei; Consort Bo bore the future Emperor Wen; Lady Qi bore Liu Ruyi, later titled the Hidden Prince of Zhao; Lady Zhao bore Liu Chang, the Fierce Prince of Huainan; and lesser consorts bore Liu You, Liu Hui, and Liu Jian, the Obscure Prince of Zhao, the Joint Prince of Zhao, and the Numinous Prince of Yan respectively.

sentences.zh: 淮南厲王長自有傳。

translations.literal: The Fierce Prince of Huainan, Chang, has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang, the Fierce Prince of Huainan, is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 齊悼惠王肥，其母高祖微時外婦也。

translations.literal: Prince Daohui of Qi, Fei—his mother was a concubine from the time before the August Ancestor Gao rose to power.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fei, Prince Daohui of Qi, was born to a woman who had been Gaozu's mistress in his humble early days.

sentences.zh: 高祖六年立，食七十餘城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of the August Ancestor Gao he was established and received more than seventy cities as his fief.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu invested him as king in the sixth year of his reign, granting him a domain of more than seventy cities.

sentences.zh: 諸民能齊言者皆與齊。

translations.literal: All people who could speak the Qi dialect were assigned to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Every household that spoke the Qi dialect was placed within his kingdom.

sentences.zh: 孝惠二年，入朝。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xiaohui he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Hui's reign he came to the capital on audience.

sentences.zh: 帝與齊王燕飲太后前，置齊王上坐，如家人禮。

translations.literal: The emperor and the king of Qi feasted and drank before the empress dowager; he seated the king of Qi in the place of honor, as in a family gathering.
translations.idiomatic: At a banquet before Empress Dowager Lü, Emperor Hui seated his half-brother, the king of Qi, in the place of honor, treating him with the easy familiarity of kin.

sentences.zh: 太后怒，乃令人酌兩卮鴆酒置前，令齊王為壽。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and had someone pour two cups of poisoned wine and set them before him, ordering the king of Qi to offer a toast.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager was furious. She had two cups of poisoned wine poured and set before the king, ordering him to offer a toast.

sentences.zh: 齊王起，帝亦起，欲俱為壽。

translations.literal: The king of Qi rose; the emperor also rose, wishing together to offer the toast.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi rose to comply, and the emperor rose as well, intending to drink with him.

sentences.zh: 太后恐，自起反卮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager feared this and herself rose and overturned the cups.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the empress dowager rose and overturned the cups herself.

sentences.zh: 齊王怪之，因不敢飲，陽醉去。

translations.literal: The king of Qi thought it strange and therefore did not dare drink; he pretended to be drunk and left.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi found the scene strange, dared not drink, and left under the pretense of drunkenness.

sentences.zh: 問知其鴆，乃憂，自以為不得脫長安。

translations.literal: On inquiry he learned it was poisoned wine; then he was anxious and thought he could not escape Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the wine had been poisoned, he grew fearful and believed he would never leave Chang'an alive.

sentences.zh: 內史士曰：「太后獨有帝與魯元公主，今王有七十餘城，而公主乃食數城。

translations.literal: The palace clerk said: "The empress dowager has only the emperor and the Princess of Lu as her own. Now Your Majesty holds more than seventy cities, while the princess receives only a few.
translations.idiomatic: A clerk of the inner administration said, "The empress dowager values only the emperor and the Princess of Lu. You hold more than seventy cities, while the princess has barely a handful.

sentences.zh: 王誠以一郡上太后為公主湯沐邑，太后必喜，王無患矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty would truly present one commandery to the empress dowager as a bath-town fief for the princess, the empress dowager will surely be pleased and Your Majesty will be without trouble."
translations.idiomatic: If you present one commandery to the empress dowager as a bath-town fief for the princess, she will be pleased and you will be safe."

sentences.zh: 於是齊王獻城陽郡以尊公主為王太后。

translations.literal: Thereupon the king of Qi presented Chengyang commandery to honor the princess as queen dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi then offered Chengyang commandery to have the princess honored as queen dowager.

sentences.zh: 呂太后喜而許之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Lü was pleased and granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lü accepted with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 乃置酒齊邸，樂飲，遣王歸國。

translations.literal: Then she set out wine at the Qi residence; they drank in merriment, and she sent the king back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: She held a feast at the Qi residence, drank in good spirits, and sent the king home.

sentences.zh: 後十三年薨，子襄嗣。

translations.literal: Thirteen years later he died; his son Xiang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He died thirteen years later, and his son Liu Xiang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 趙隱王如意，九年立。

translations.literal: The Hidden Prince of Zhao, Ruyi, was established in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ruyi, posthumously known as the Hidden Prince of Zhao, was invested as king in the ninth year of Gaozu's reign.

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖崩，呂太后徵王到長安，鴆殺之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the August Ancestor Gao died; Empress Dowager Lü summoned the king to Chang'an and killed him with poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Emperor Hui's reign, after Gaozu had died, Empress Dowager Lü summoned Prince Ruyi to Chang'an and murdered him with poisoned wine.

sentences.zh: 無子，絕。

translations.literal: He had no sons; the line was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir, and his house came to an end.

sentences.zh: 趙幽王友，十一年立為淮陽王。

translations.literal: Prince You of Zhao the Obscure—in the eleventh year was established as king of Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You, later known as Prince You of Zhao the Obscure, was invested as king of Huaiyang in the eleventh year.

sentences.zh: 趙隱王如意死，孝惠元年，徙友王趙，凡立十四年。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Prince of Zhao, Ruyi, died, in the first year of Xiaohui, You was moved to be king of Zhao; in all he reigned fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Ruyi, the Hidden Prince of Zhao, was killed, Liu You was transferred to Zhao in the first year of Emperor Hui's reign and ruled there for fourteen years in all.

sentences.zh: 友以諸呂女為后，不愛，愛它姬。

translations.literal: You took a daughter of the Lü clan as queen but did not love her; he loved another lady.
translations.idiomatic: He took a Lü clanswoman as queen but favored another consort instead.

sentences.zh: 諸呂女怒去，讒之於太后曰：「王曰『呂氏安得王？

translations.literal: The Lü clanswoman left in anger and slandered him to the empress dowager, saying: "The king said, 'How can the Lü clan have kings?
translations.idiomatic: The queen stormed off and denounced him to the empress dowager, saying, "The king declared, 'How can the Lü clan hold royal titles?

sentences.zh: 太后百歲後，吾必擊之。』」

translations.literal: After the empress dowager passes her hundred years, I will surely strike them.'"
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager is gone, I will attack them.'"

sentences.zh: 太后怒，以故召趙王。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was angry and for this reason summoned the king of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the empress dowager summoned the king of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 趙王至，置邸不見，令衛圍守之，不得食。

translations.literal: When the king of Zhao arrived, he was lodged at a residence but not received; guards were ordered to surround and hold him, and he was given no food.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, he was lodged at a residence but denied audience; guards surrounded the building and cut off his food.

sentences.zh: 其群臣或竊饋之，輒捕論之。

translations.literal: Some of his ministers secretly brought him food; they were immediately seized and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who tried to smuggle food to him were seized and punished.

sentences.zh: 趙王餓，乃歌曰：「諸呂用事兮，劉氏微；

translations.literal: The king of Zhao, starving, then sang: "The Lü clan holds power; the house of Liu is enfeebled;
translations.idiomatic: Starving, the king of Zhao sang: "The Lü clan holds power; the house of Liu grows weak;

sentences.zh: 迫脅王侯兮，彊授我妃。

translations.literal: They coerce kings and marquises and forcibly give me a queen.
translations.idiomatic: They coerce kings and marquises and force a queen upon me.

sentences.zh: 我妃既妒兮，誣我以惡；

translations.literal: My queen is jealous and falsely accuses me of evil;
translations.idiomatic: My queen, jealous, slanders me with false crimes;

sentences.zh: 讒女亂國兮，上曾不寤。

translations.literal: The slandering woman throws the state into disorder, yet the sovereign never awakens to it.
translations.idiomatic: a slandering woman throws the realm into chaos, yet the throne never awakens.

sentences.zh: 我無忠臣兮，何故棄國？

translations.literal: I have no loyal ministers—why should I be made to abandon my state?
translations.idiomatic: I have no loyal ministers—why must I be driven from my kingdom?

sentences.zh: 自快中野兮，蒼天與直！

translations.literal: Let me find release in the open wilds; may Heaven grant me justice!
translations.idiomatic: Let me find release in the open wilds; may Heaven grant me justice!

sentences.zh: 于嗟不可悔兮，寧早自賊！

translations.literal: Alas, what cannot be undone—better to destroy myself early!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, what cannot be undone—better to die by my own hand!

sentences.zh: 為王餓死兮，誰者憐之？

translations.literal: To die of hunger as a king—who will pity me?
translations.idiomatic: To die of hunger as a king—who will pity me?

sentences.zh: 呂氏絕理兮，託天報仇！」

translations.literal: The Lü clan violates all right principle; I entrust vengeance to Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: The Lü clan violates all right principle; I entrust vengeance to Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 遂幽死。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died under confinement.
translations.idiomatic: He died under confinement.

sentences.zh: 以民禮葬之長安。

translations.literal: He was buried in Chang'an with commoner rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in Chang'an with the rites due a commoner.

sentences.zh: 高后崩，孝文即位，立幽王子遂為趙王。

translations.literal: When Empress Gao died, Xiaowen ascended the throne and established Prince You's son Sui as king of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Lü died and Emperor Wen took the throne, Liu You's son Liu Sui was invested as king of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 二年，有司請立皇子為王。

translations.literal: In the second year, the responsible offices requested that imperial sons be established as kings.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the responsible offices petitioned to invest the emperor's sons as kings.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「趙幽王幽死，朕甚憐之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Prince You of Zhao the Obscure died under confinement; We are deeply moved with pity.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Prince You of Zhao died under confinement, and We are deeply grieved.

sentences.zh: 已立其長子遂為趙王。

translations.literal: We have already established his eldest son Sui as king of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: We have already invested his eldest son Liu Sui as king of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 遂弟辟彊及齊悼惠王子朱虛侯章、東牟侯興居有功，皆可王。」

translations.literal: Sui's younger brother Pijiang, and Zhang, Marquis of Zhuxu, and Xingju, Marquis of Dongmou—sons of Prince Daohui of Qi—have merit and may all be made kings."
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Liu Pijiang, together with Liu Zhang, Marquis of Zhuxu, and Liu Xingju, Marquis of Dongmou—sons of Prince Daohui of Qi—have all earned the right to royal investiture."

sentences.zh: 於是取趙之河間立辟彊，是為河間文王。

translations.literal: Thereupon the territory of Hejian in Zhao was taken to establish Pijiang; this is Prince Wen of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Hejian was carved from Zhao and given to Liu Pijiang, who became Prince Wen of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 文王立十三年薨，子哀王福嗣。

translations.literal: Prince Wen reigned thirteen years and died; his son Prince Ai Fu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wen ruled thirteen years and died; his son Liu Fu, Prince Ai, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 一年薨。

translations.literal: After one year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after one year.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: He had no sons; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no heir, and the kingdom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 趙王遂立二十六年，孝景時晁錯以過削趙常山郡，諸侯怨，吳楚反，遂與合謀起兵。

translations.literal: King Liu Sui of Zhao had reigned twenty-six years. In the time of Emperor Xiaojing, Chao Cuo, citing faults, stripped Zhao of the Changshan commandery; the feudal lords resented it; Wu and Chu rebelled, and Sui joined them in plotting to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sui had been king of Zhao for twenty-six years when, under Emperor Jing, Chao Cuo seized the Changshan commandery from Zhao as punishment for alleged wrongdoing. The kingdoms were already smoldering with resentment; when Wu and Chu rose in revolt, Liu Sui conspired with them and mobilized his own forces.

sentences.zh: 其相建德、內史王悍諫，不聽。

translations.literal: His chancellor Jiande and his interior secretary Wang Han remonstrated; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His chancellor Jiande and interior secretary Wang Han urged him to reconsider, but he refused to heed them.

sentences.zh: 遂燒殺德、悍，發兵住其西界，欲待吳楚俱進，北使匈奴與連和。

translations.literal: Sui then had Jiande and Han burned to death, sent troops to hold his western frontier, wished to wait until Wu and Chu advanced together, and sent envoys north to the Xiongnu to conclude an alliance.
translations.idiomatic: He had Jiande and Wang Han executed by fire, deployed troops along his western border to await a joint advance with Wu and Chu, and sent a mission north to court an alliance with the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 漢使曲周侯酈寄擊之，趙王城守邯鄲，相距七月。

translations.literal: The Han dispatched Marquis of Quzhou Li Ji to attack him; the King of Zhao defended Handan; they faced each other seven months.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Marquis of Quzhou Li Ji against him. The king of Zhao shut himself inside Handan, and the siege lasted seven months.

sentences.zh: 吳楚敗，匈奴聞之，亦不肯入邊。

translations.literal: When Wu and Chu were defeated, the Xiongnu heard of it and would not enter the border either.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu and Chu collapsed, the Xiongnu, learning the outcome, likewise declined to cross the frontier.

sentences.zh: 欒布自破齊還，并兵引水灌趙城。

translations.literal: Luan Bu, returning from having crushed Qi, combined forces, led water in, and flooded the Zhao city.
translations.idiomatic: Luan Bo, returning from the campaign that had broken Qi, joined his command with others, diverted a river, and inundated the Zhao capital.

sentences.zh: 城壞，王遂自殺，國除。

translations.literal: The walls gave way; King Sui killed himself; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The ramparts failed; Liu Sui took his own life, and the kingdom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 景帝憐趙相、內史守正死，皆封其子為列侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing pitied the Zhao chancellor and interior secretary who had died upholding what was right, and enfeoffed both their sons as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Touched by the loyalty of the Zhao chancellor and interior secretary who had died for their principles, Emperor Jing made each man's son a full marquis.

sentences.zh: 趙共王

translations.literal: Prince Hui of Zhao the Joint
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui of Zhao the Joint

sentences.zh: 趙共王恢。

translations.literal: Prince Hui of Zhao, Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui, the Joint Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 十一年，梁王彭越誅，立恢為梁王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, King Peng Yue of Liang was executed, and Hui was established as king of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Gaozu's reign, after Peng Yue, king of Liang, was put to death, Liu Hui was transferred to Liang and invested there.

sentences.zh: 十六年，趙幽王死，呂后徙恢王趙，恢心不樂。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, Prince You of Zhao the Obscure died; Empress Lü moved Hui to be king of Zhao; Hui's heart was not glad.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, when Prince You of Zhao died, Empress Lü reassigned Liu Hui to Zhao. He went unwillingly, his heart heavy at the move.

sentences.zh: 太后以呂產女為趙王后，王后從官皆諸呂也，內擅權，微司趙王，王不得自恣。

translations.literal: The empress dowager took Lü Chan's daughter as queen of Zhao; the queen's attendants were all of the Lü clan; within they monopolized power, secretly watched the king of Zhao, and the king could not follow his own will.
translations.idiomatic: She married him to a daughter of Lü Chan, whose entire household staff were Lü partisans. They seized the inner court, spied on the king at every turn, and left him unable to live as he pleased.

sentences.zh: 王有愛姬，王后鴆殺之。

translations.literal: The king had a beloved concubine; the queen killed her with poisoned wine.
translations.idiomatic: When he favored another woman, his Lü queen poisoned her.

sentences.zh: 王乃為歌詩四章，令樂人歌之。

translations.literal: The king then composed four stanzas of song-poetry and ordered musicians to sing them.
translations.idiomatic: In his grief he wrote four songs and had the court musicians perform them.

sentences.zh: 王悲思，六月自殺。

translations.literal: The king was sorrowful and brooding; in the sixth month he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Brokenhearted, he took his own life in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 太后聞之，以為用婦人故自殺，無思奉宗廟禮，廢其嗣。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager heard of it, she thought that because of a woman he had killed himself, without thought for the rites owed the ancestral temple; she abolished his posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager dismissed his death as the act of a man who had killed himself over a woman and showed no regard for his duty to the imperial ancestors; she struck his line from the succession.

sentences.zh: 燕靈王建。

translations.literal: Prince Jian of Yan the Numinous.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian, Prince Jian of Yan the Numinous.

sentences.zh: 十一年，燕王盧綰亡入匈奴，明年，立建為燕王。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the king of Yan, Lu Wan, fled and entered the Xiongnu; the next year Jian was established as king of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Lu Wan, king of Yan, fled to the Xiongnu; the following year Liu Jian was invested as king of Yan.

sentences.zh: 十五年薨，有美人子，太后使人殺之，絕後。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died. He had a son by a beautiful woman; the empress dowager sent men to kill the child, and the line was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year. He had left a son by a favored consort, but the empress dowager had the child killed, and the line ended.

sentences.zh: 齊悼惠王子，前後凡九人為王：太子襄為齊哀王，次子章為城陽景王，興居為濟北王，將閭為齊王，志為濟北王，辟光為濟南王，賢為菑川王，卬為膠西王，雄渠為膠東王。

translations.literal: The sons of Prince Daohui of Qi, in all before and after, nine men became kings: the heir Xiang was Prince Ai of Qi; the second son Zhang was Prince Jing of Chengyang; Xingju was king of Jibei; Jianglü was king of Qi; Zhi was king of Jibei; Piguang was king of Jinan; Xian was king of Zichuan; Ang was king of Jiaoxi; Xiongqu was king of Jiaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Daohui of Qi left nine sons who in turn received royal titles: the crown prince Xiang became Prince Ai of Qi; Liu Zhang became Prince Jing of Chengyang; Liu Xingju, king of Jibei; Liu Jianglü, king of Qi; Liu Zhi, again king of Jibei; Liu Piguang of Jinan; Liu Xian of Zichuan; Liu Ang of Jiaoxi; and Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong.

sentences.zh: 齊哀王襄，孝惠六年嗣立。

translations.literal: Prince Ai of Qi, Xiang—in the sixth year of Xiaohui succeeded and was established.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang, Prince Ai of Qi, succeeded in the sixth year of Emperor Hui's reign.

sentences.zh: 明年，惠帝崩，呂太后稱制。

translations.literal: The next year Emperor Hui died; Empress Dowager Lü assumed regency.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Hui died, and Empress Dowager Lü assumed regency.

sentences.zh: 元年，以其兄子鄜侯呂台為呂王，割齊之濟南郡為呂王奉邑。

translations.literal: In the first year of her regency she made her elder brother's son Lü Tai, Marquis of Fu, king of Lü, and carved Jinan commandery from Qi as the fief of the king of Lü.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of her regency she made her nephew Lü Tai, Marquis of Fu, king of Lü and carved Jinan commandery from Qi as his fief.

sentences.zh: 明年，哀王弟章入宿衛於漢，高后封為朱虛侯，以呂祿女妻之。

translations.literal: The next year Prince Ai's younger brother Zhang entered palace guard service at the Han court; Empress Gao enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhuxu and gave him Lü Lu's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Liu Zhang, the prince's younger brother, entered guard service at the Han court; Empress Dowager Lü enfeoffed him as Marquis of Zhuxu and married him to Lü Lu's daughter.

sentences.zh: 後四年，封章弟興居為東牟侯，皆宿衛長安。

translations.literal: Four years later she enfeoffed Zhang's younger brother Xingju as Marquis of Dongmou; both guarded Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later she enfeoffed Liu Xingju, Zhang's younger brother, as Marquis of Dongmou; both brothers served on guard duty in Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高后七年，割齊琅邪郡，立營陵侯劉澤為琅邪王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Empress Gao she carved Langye commandery from Qi and established Liu Ze, Marquis of Yingling, as king of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of her regency she carved Langye commandery from Qi and made Liu Ze, Marquis of Yingling, king of Langye.

sentences.zh: 是歲，趙王友幽死于邸。

translations.literal: That year Prince You of Zhao died under confinement at his lodging.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Liu You, king of Zhao, died under confinement at his lodging.

sentences.zh: 三趙王既廢，高后立諸呂為三王，擅權用事。

translations.literal: After the three kings of Zhao had been removed, Empress Gao established various Lü clansmen as three kings and monopolized power.
translations.idiomatic: After the three Zhao kings had been eliminated, she invested three Lü clansmen as kings and seized power for her kin.

sentences.zh: 章年二十，有氣力，忿劉氏不得職。

translations.literal: Zhang was twenty years old, had strength and vigor, and resented that the Liu house did not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang was twenty, strong and hot-tempered, and bitter that real power lay not with the house of Liu.

sentences.zh: 嘗入侍燕飲，高后令章為酒吏。

translations.literal: Once when he entered attendance at a banquet of drinking and entertainment, Empress Gao ordered Zhang to be wine steward.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he attended one of Empress Lü's feasts, and she put him in charge of the wine.

sentences.zh: 章自請曰：「臣，將種也，請得以軍法行酒。」

translations.literal: Zhang himself requested, saying, "I, your servant, am of a general's stock; I beg to conduct the wine by military law."
translations.idiomatic: He volunteered: "I am a soldier's son. Permit me to enforce the drinking rules as if we were under military law."

sentences.zh: 高后曰：「可。」

translations.literal: Empress Gao said: "It may be so."
translations.idiomatic: "Very well," said Empress Lü.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，章進歌舞，已而曰：「請為太后言耕田。」

translations.literal: When the wine was warm, Zhang advanced song and dance, and afterward said: "I beg to speak to the empress dowager of plowing fields."
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was warm, Zhang advanced song and dance, and afterward said: "I beg to speak to the empress dowager of plowing fields."

sentences.zh: 高后兒子畜之，笑曰：「顧乃父知田耳，若生而為王子，安知田乎？」

translations.literal: Empress Gao doted on him as a child and laughed, saying: "Only your father knew fields; you were born a king's son—how would you know fields?"
translations.idiomatic: She doted on him like a son and laughed. "Your father knew the plow; you were born a prince of the blood. What could you know of the soil?"

sentences.zh: 章曰：「臣知之。」

translations.literal: Zhang said: "Your servant knows it."
translations.idiomatic: "I know it," said Liu Zhang.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「試為我言田意。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Try for me to speak the meaning of fields."
translations.idiomatic: "Then tell me what you know of the field," she said.

sentences.zh: 章曰：「深耕穊種，立苗欲疏；

translations.literal: Zhang said: "Deep plowing and dense sowing; setting seedlings one desires sparse;
translations.idiomatic: "Plow deep and sow thick," he began; "set the seedlings far apart—

sentences.zh: 非其種者，鉏而去之。」

translations.literal: What is not of its kind, hoe it out and remove it."
translations.idiomatic: —and whatever is not your own strain, hoe it up and cast it away."

sentences.zh: 太后默然。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager fell silent.

sentences.zh: 頃之，諸呂有一人醉，亡酒，章追，拔劍斬之，而還報曰：「有亡酒一人，臣謹行軍法斬之。」

translations.literal: Before long, one of the Lü men was drunk, fled the wine, Zhang pursued him, drew his sword and beheaded him, and returning reported: "There was one who fled the wine; your servant, respectfully applying military law, has beheaded him."
translations.idiomatic: Presently one of the Lü guests broke the rules and tried to slip away. Liu Zhang ran him down, cut off his head, and reported back: "One man deserted his cup. I have executed him under military law."

sentences.zh: 太后左右大驚。

translations.literal: Those to the left and right of the empress dowager were greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's attendants cried out in alarm.

sentences.zh: 業已許其軍法，亡以罪也。

translations.literal: Already they had permitted him military law; there was no way to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: She had already authorized military discipline; there was no honest pretext on which to punish him.

sentences.zh: 因罷酒。

translations.literal: Thereupon they stopped the wine.
translations.idiomatic: The banquet broke up at once.

sentences.zh: 自是後，諸呂憚章，雖大臣皆依朱虛侯。

translations.literal: From this afterward, the Lü feared Zhang; even great ministers leaned on the Marquis of Zhuxu.
translations.idiomatic: After that the Lü clan feared Liu Zhang, and even senior ministers looked to the Marquis of Zhuxu for leadership.

sentences.zh: 劉氏為彊。

translations.literal: The Liu house became strong.
translations.idiomatic: The house of Liu gathered strength again.

sentences.zh: 其明年，高后崩。

translations.literal: The next year, Empress Gao died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Empress Lü died.

sentences.zh: 趙王呂祿為上將軍，呂王產為相國，皆居長安中，聚兵以威大臣，欲為亂。

translations.literal: King Lü Lu of Zhao was senior general; King Lü Chan was chancellor; both dwelt in Chang'an, gathered troops to awe the great ministers, and wished to make rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Lu, king of Zhao, held the post of senior general; Lü Chan, king of Lü, was chancellor. Both remained in Chang'an, massed troops to overawe the ministers, and plotted revolt.

sentences.zh: 章以呂祿女為婦，知其謀，乃使人陰出告其兄齊王，欲令發兵西，朱虛侯、東牟侯欲從中與大臣為內應，以誅諸呂，因立齊王為帝。

translations.literal: Zhang took Lü Lu's daughter as wife, knew their plot, then sent men secretly out to inform his brother the king of Qi, wishing to have him raise troops westward; the Marquis of Zhuxu and the Marquis of Dongmou wished from within to join with the great ministers as inner response, in order to execute the Lü, and thereby establish the king of Qi as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zhang was married to Lü Lu's daughter, he learned of the conspiracy and secretly warned his brother, the king of Qi, urging him to march west while he and his cousin, the Marquis of Dongmou, coordinated with loyal ministers inside the capital to extirpate the Lü and set the king of Qi on the throne.

sentences.zh: 齊王聞此計，與其舅駟鈞、郎中令祝午、中尉魏勃陰謀發兵。

translations.literal: The king of Qi heard this plan, and with his maternal uncle Si Jun, palace superintendent Zhu Wu, and commandant Wei Bo secretly plotted to raise troops.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi took counsel in secret with his uncle Si Jun, his palace superintendent Zhu Wu, and commandant Wei Bo, and plotted to raise troops.

sentences.zh: 齊相召平聞之，乃發兵入衛王宮。

translations.literal: The chancellor of Qi, Shao Ping, heard of it, then raised troops to enter and guard the royal palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Shao Ping of Qi got wind of it, he called out the guard and sealed the royal palace.

sentences.zh: 魏勃紿平曰：「王欲發兵，非有漢虎符驗也。

translations.literal: Wei Bo deceived Ping, saying: "The king wishes to raise troops, yet there is no verification by Han tiger tallies.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo lied to him: "The king means to rebel without the court's tiger tallies.

sentences.zh: 而相君圍王，固善。

translations.literal: Yet the chancellor besieges the king—indeed it is good.
translations.idiomatic: You have wisely surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 勃請為君將兵衛衛王。」

translations.literal: Bo begs to take for you command of troops to guard the king."
translations.idiomatic: Let me relieve you: give me the troops, and I will garrison the palace in your stead."

sentences.zh: 召平信之，乃使魏勃將。

translations.literal: Shao Ping trusted him, then sent Wei Bo to command.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Ping believed him and handed over the command.

sentences.zh: 勃既將，以兵圍相府。

translations.literal: Bo, having taken command, used troops to surround the chancellor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo at once turned the same troops against the chancellor's compound and besieged it.

sentences.zh: 召平曰：「嗟乎！

translations.literal: Shao Ping said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: "Alas," cried Shao Ping,

sentences.zh: 道家之言『當斷不斷，反受其亂』。」

translations.literal: The words of the Daoists: 'When one ought to decide and does not, one instead receives disorder.'"
translations.idiomatic: the Daoists had it right: hesitate when you must act, and chaos finds you instead."

sentences.zh: 遂自殺。

translations.literal: Thereupon he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: He killed himself on the spot.

sentences.zh: 於是齊王以駟鈞為相，魏勃為將軍，祝午為內史，悉發國中兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon the king of Qi took Si Jun as chancellor, Wei Bo as general, Zhu Wu as interior secretary, and fully raised the troops of the state.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi then named Si Jun chancellor, Wei Bo general, and Zhu Wu interior secretary, and mobilized every able-bodied man in the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 使祝午紿琅邪王曰：「呂氏為亂，齊王發兵欲西誅之。

translations.literal: He sent Zhu Wu to deceive the king of Langye, saying: "The Lü are in rebellion; the king of Qi has raised troops wishing to go west and execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wu was sent with a tale for the king of Langye: "The Lü have turned traitor; the king of Qi is marching west to punish them.

sentences.zh: 齊王自以兒子，年少，不習兵革之事，願舉國委大王。

translations.literal: The king of Qi, considering himself a young son, young in years, not practiced in matters of armor and weapons, wishes to entrust the whole state to the great king.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi, declaring himself young and untried in war, begs to place the entire army under your command.

sentences.zh: 大王自高帝將也，習戰事。

translations.literal: The great king from the time of the August Emperor was a general, practiced in warfare.
translations.idiomatic: You commanded troops for Emperor Gao and know the field.

sentences.zh: 齊王不敢離兵，使臣請大王幸之臨菑見齊王計事，并將齊兵以西平關中之亂。」

translations.literal: The king of Qi does not dare leave the troops; he sends your servant to request the great king, if you would be so kind, to come to Linzi to meet the king of Qi to plan affairs, and together lead the troops of Qi west to pacify the disorders within the passes."
translations.idiomatic: He cannot leave his host, so he asks you to ride to Linzi, meet with him, plan affairs, and lead the troops of Qi west to settle the turmoil in Guanzhong."

sentences.zh: 琅邪王信之，以為然，乃馳見齊王。

translations.literal: The king of Langye trusted it, thought it so, then galloped to see the king of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Langye believed him, thought it was so, and galloped off to see the king of Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊王與魏勃等因留琅邪王，而使祝午盡發琅邪國而并將其兵。

translations.literal: The king of Qi, with Wei Bo and others, therefore detained the king of Langye, and sent Zhu Wu to fully raise Langye's state and together command its troops.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi and his confederates held him fast while Zhu Wu stripped Langye of its remaining troops and brought them under Qi's banner.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王劉澤既欺，不得反國，乃說齊王曰：「齊悼惠王，高皇帝長子也，推本言之，大王高皇帝適長孫也，當立。

translations.literal: King Liu Ze of Langye, having been deceived, could not return to his state, then persuaded the king of Qi, saying: "Prince Daohui of Qi was the August Emperor Gao's eldest son; tracing the root in speaking, the great king is the August Emperor Gao's eldest grandson by the proper wife; he ought to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ze, king of Langye, was trapped in Qi and argued: "Prince Daohui was Gaozu's eldest son; by strict descent you are Gaozu's senior grandson by the main line and have the strongest claim to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今諸大臣狐疑未有所定，而澤於劉氏最為長年，大臣固待澤決計。

translations.literal: Now the great ministers hesitate and have not yet decided, and Ze among the Liu is the eldest in years; the great ministers certainly await Ze to decide the plan.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers in Chang'an still waver, and I am the oldest living prince of the blood; they will listen when I speak.

sentences.zh: 今大王留臣無為也，不如使我入關計事。」

translations.literal: Now the great king detaining your servant accomplishes nothing; it would be better to let me enter the passes to plan affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Keeping me here serves no purpose. Send me through the passes to settle the succession in your favor."

sentences.zh: 齊王以為然，乃益具車送琅邪王。

translations.literal: The king of Qi thought it so, then increased carriages and saw off the king of Langye.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi thought this was so, then furnished additional carriages and escorted the king of Langye on his way.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王既行，齊遂舉兵西攻呂國之濟南。

translations.literal: Once the king of Langye had departed, Qi then raised troops and marched west to attack Jinan, the domain of the king of Lü.
translations.idiomatic: After the king of Langye had set out, Qi raised troops and marched west against Jinan, the fief of the Lü king.

sentences.zh: 於是齊王遺諸侯王書曰：「高帝平定天下，王諸子弟。

translations.literal: Thereupon the king of Qi sent a letter to the feudal kings, saying: "The August Emperor Gao pacified the realm and enfeoffed his sons and younger brothers as kings.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi then sent a letter to the other feudal kings, saying, "The High Emperor pacified the realm and enfeoffed his sons and younger brothers as kings.

sentences.zh: 悼惠王薨，惠帝使留侯張良立臣為齊王。

translations.literal: When Prince Daohui died, Emperor Hui sent Marquis of Liuhou Zhang Liang to establish me as king of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Daohui died, Emperor Hui sent Zhang Liang, Marquis of Liuhou, to invest me as king of Qi.

sentences.zh: 惠帝崩，高后用事，春秋高，聽諸呂擅廢帝更立，又殺三趙王，滅梁、趙、燕，以王諸呂，分齊國為四。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui died; Empress Gao took power. Her years were advanced, yet she listened as the Lü clan arbitrarily deposed emperors and set up others, again killed the three kings of Zhao, extinguished Liang, Zhao, and Yan, and made various Lü clansmen kings, dividing Qi into four parts.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Hui died, Empress Dowager Lü took power. Though advanced in years, she allowed the Lü clan to depose emperors and set up others, killed the three Zhao kings, extinguished Liang, Zhao, and Yan, invested Lü clansmen as kings, and carved Qi into four parts.

sentences.zh: 忠臣進諫，上或亂不聽。

translations.literal: Loyal ministers offered remonstrance, but the sovereign, perhaps confused, would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal ministers remonstrated, but the throne, perhaps confused, would not listen.

sentences.zh: 今高后崩，皇帝春秋富，未能治天下，固待大臣諸侯。

translations.literal: Now Empress Gao has died; the emperor is young in years and cannot yet govern the realm—he surely relies on great ministers and feudal kings.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the empress dowager is dead, the emperor is still young and cannot yet govern the realm; he surely relies on great ministers and the feudal kings.

sentences.zh: 今諸呂又擅自尊官，聚官嚴威，劫列侯忠臣，撟制以令天下，宗廟以危。

translations.literal: Now the Lü clan again arrogantly appoint themselves to offices, gather offices to display stern authority, coerce the ranked marquises and loyal ministers, and falsify commands to rule the realm, putting the ancestral temple in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Lü clan again arrogates offices to themselves, amasses power, coerces ranked marquises and loyal ministers, and falsifies commands to rule the realm, putting the ancestral temple in peril.

sentences.zh: 寡人帥兵入誅不當為王者。」

translations.literal: I shall lead troops within the passes to execute those who ought not to be kings."
translations.idiomatic: I shall lead troops within the passes to execute those who ought not to be kings."

sentences.zh: 漢聞之，相國呂產等遣大將軍潁陰侯灌嬰將兵擊之。

translations.literal: When the Han heard of it, Chancellor Lü Chan and others dispatched Grand General Marquis of Yingyin Guan Ying to lead troops and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned of the rising and ordered Grand General Guan Ying, Marquis of Yingyin, to take the field against Qi.

sentences.zh: 嬰至滎陽，乃謀曰：「諸呂舉兵關中，欲危劉氏而自立，今我破齊還報，是益呂氏資也。」

translations.literal: When Guan Ying reached Xingyang, he plotted, saying: "The Lü have raised troops within the passes, wishing to endanger the Liu and establish themselves; now if I break Qi and return to report, this increases the Lü's resources."
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyang he halted and reasoned with his officers: "The Lü hold Guanzhong and mean to supplant the Liu. If I crush Qi and march home, I only strengthen their hand."

sentences.zh: 乃留兵屯滎陽，使人諭齊王及諸侯，與連和，以待呂氏之變而共誅之。

translations.literal: Then he left troops garrisoned at Xingyang, sent men to instruct the king of Qi and the feudal lords, joined in alliance with them, and waited for the Lü's coup in order together to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: He camped at Xingyang, sent envoys to the king of Qi and the other kings, and forged a common front to wait for the Lü to move, then strike them down together.

sentences.zh: 齊王聞之，乃屯兵西界待約。

translations.literal: The king of Qi heard it, then garrisoned troops on the western border awaiting the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi drew up his army on his western frontier to await the signal.

sentences.zh: 呂祿、呂產欲作亂，朱虛侯章與太尉勃、丞相平等誅之。

translations.literal: Lü Lu and Lü Chan wished to make rebellion; Marquis of Zhuxu Zhang with Grand Commandant Bo, Chancellor Ping, and others executed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Lu and Lü Chan moved toward open revolt, Liu Zhang joined Zhou Bo, Chen Ping, and the loyal ministers in cutting them down.

sentences.zh: 章首先斬呂產，太尉勃等乃盡誅諸呂。

translations.literal: Zhang first beheaded Lü Chan; Grand Commandant Bo and others then fully executed the Lü.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang struck the first blow, killing Lü Chan; Zhou Bo and the rest then wiped out the entire Lü faction.

sentences.zh: 而琅邪王亦從齊至長安。

translations.literal: And the king of Langye also came from Qi to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Liu Ze had traveled from Qi to Chang'an as well.

sentences.zh: 大臣議欲立齊王，皆曰：「母家駟鈞惡戾，虎而冠者也。

translations.literal: The great ministers deliberated wishing to establish the king of Qi; all said: "The mother's family Si Jun is cruel and perverse, a tiger wearing a cap.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers first considered the king of Qi, but objected in one voice: "His uncle Si Jun is vicious and overbearing—a man with a tiger's heart beneath a courtier's hat.

sentences.zh: 訪以呂氏故，幾亂天下，今又立齊王，是欲復為呂氏也。

translations.literal: By the cause of the Lü, they nearly threw the realm into chaos; now again to establish the king of Qi is to wish again to make a Lü.
translations.idiomatic: The Lü rose from a mother's clan and nearly destroyed the dynasty; to enthrone Qi now would be to invite another Lü.

sentences.zh: 代王母家薄氏，君子長者，且代王，高帝子，於今見在，最為長。

translations.literal: The king of Dai's mother's family, the Bo, are gentlemen and elders; moreover the king of Dai, a son of August Emperor Gao, among those now living is the eldest.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Dai’s maternal family, the Bo clan, are gentlemen and elders; moreover the king of Dai is a son of the High Emperor, is still living today, and is the eldest.

sentences.zh: 以子則順，以善人則大臣安。」

translations.literal: By the standard of proper sonship it is orderly; by choosing a good man the great ministers will be secure."
translations.idiomatic: Succession among the sons would be orderly, and a worthy prince would put the ministers at ease."

sentences.zh: 於是大臣乃謀迎代王，而遣章以誅呂氏事告齊王，令罷兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon the great ministers then plotted to welcome the king of Dai, and dispatched Zhang to inform the king of Qi of the affair of executing the Lü, ordering him to disband the troops.
translations.idiomatic: They therefore resolved to welcome Liu Heng of Dai, sent Liu Zhang to tell his brother in Qi that the Lü were dead, and ordered him to stand down.

sentences.zh: 灌嬰在滎陽，聞魏勃本教齊王反，既誅呂氏，罷齊兵，使使召責問魏勃。

translations.literal: Guan Ying was at Xingyang; he heard that Wei Bo had originally instructed the king of Qi to rebel; after the Lü had been executed and Qi troops disbanded, he sent envoys to summon and rebuke Wei Bo.
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ying, still at Xingyang, had heard that Wei Bo had instigated the king of Qi's revolt. Once the Lü were gone and Qi's army sent home, he summoned Wei Bo to account for himself.

sentences.zh: 勃曰：「失火之家，豈暇先言丈人後救火乎！」

translations.literal: Bo said: "In a house on fire, how is there leisure first to speak to the elders and afterward fight the fire!"
translations.idiomatic: "When the roof is burning," Wei Bo replied, "do you first bow to your elders or grab a bucket?"

sentences.zh: 因退立，股戰而栗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he withdrew and stood; his thighs trembled and he shivered.
translations.idiomatic: He stepped back, legs trembling, unable to steady himself.

sentences.zh: 恐不能言者，終無他語。

translations.literal: Fearing he could not speak, in the end he had no other words.
translations.idiomatic: Too frightened to say more, he offered no further defense.

sentences.zh: 灌將軍孰視，笑曰：「人謂魏勃勇，妄庸人耳，何能為乎！」

translations.literal: General Guan stared long, laughed, and said: "People call Wei Bo brave—he is merely a foolish common fellow; what can he do!"
translations.idiomatic: Guan Ying studied him a long moment, then laughed. "They say Wei Bo is bold. The man is a panicky fool—harmless."

sentences.zh: 乃罷勃。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dismissed Bo.
translations.idiomatic: He let Wei Bo go.

sentences.zh: 勃父以善鼓琴見秦皇帝。

translations.literal: Bo's father, by being good at drumming the zither, was received by the Qin August Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo's father had won an audience with the First Emperor of Qin by his skill on the zither.

sentences.zh: 及勃少時，欲求見齊相曹參，家貧無以自通，乃常獨早埽齊相舍人門外。

translations.literal: When Bo was young, he wished to seek an audience with Chancellor Cao Shen of Qi; his family was poor and had no means to introduce himself; therefore he often alone early swept outside the gate of the chancellor of Qi's retainer.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth, wanting to meet Chancellor Cao Shen of Qi but too poor for an introduction, he rose before dawn day after day to sweep the doorstep of one of the chancellor's retainers.

sentences.zh: 舍人怪之，以為物而司之，得勃。

translations.literal: The retainer thought it strange, thought it a spirit and watched for it, and caught Bo.
translations.idiomatic: The retainer thought some ghost was at work and lay in wait until he caught Wei Bo in the act.

sentences.zh: 勃曰：「願見相君，無因，故為子埽，欲以求見。」

translations.literal: Bo said: "I wish to see the chancellor; having no means of access, therefore I sweep for you, wishing thereby to seek an audience."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo said, "I beg an audience with the chancellor, but I have no way in. That is why I have been sweeping your doorstep—to earn a chance to meet him."

sentences.zh: 於是舍人見勃，曹參因以為舍人。

translations.literal: Thereupon the retainer received Wei Bo, and Cao Shen accordingly took him on as a retainer.
translations.idiomatic: The retainer then received Wei Bo, and Cao Shen took him on as a retainer.

sentences.zh: 壹為參御言事，以為賢，言之悼惠王。

translations.literal: Once when he attended Cao Shen in reporting affairs, Cao Shen thought him worthy and spoke of him to Prince Daohui.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while attending Cao Shen in reporting affairs, he impressed the chancellor as capable, and Cao Shen recommended him to Prince Daohui.

sentences.zh: 王召見，拜為內史。

translations.literal: The prince summoned him for audience and appointed him Director of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The prince summoned him and appointed him Director of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 始悼惠王得自置二千石。

translations.literal: This was when Prince Daohui first gained the right to appoint officials of two-thousand-bushel rank on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: This was when Prince Daohui first gained the right to appoint officials of two-thousand-bushel rank on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 及悼惠王薨，哀王嗣，勃用事重於相。

translations.literal: When Prince Daohui died, Prince Ai succeeded, and Wei Bo wielded power weightier than the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Daohui died and Prince Ai succeeded, Wei Bo wielded power greater than the chancellor's.

sentences.zh: 齊王既罷兵歸，而代王立，是為孝文帝。

translations.literal: The king of Qi having disbanded the troops and returned, the king of Dai was established; this is Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Qi sent his men home; Liu Heng of Dai ascended the throne as Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 文帝元年，盡以高后時所割齊之城陽、琅邪、濟南郡復予齊，而徙琅邪王王燕。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Wen, all the territories cut from Qi during Empress Gao's time—Chengyang, Langye, and Jinan commanderies—were restored to Qi, and the king of Langye was moved to rule Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Emperor Wen's reign, Chengyang, Langye, and Jinan—the commanderies carved from Qi under Empress Dowager Lü—were all restored to Qi, and the king of Langye was transferred to rule Yan.

sentences.zh: 益封朱虛侯、東牟侯各二千戶，黃金千斤。

translations.literal: Additional fiefs of two thousand households and a thousand jin of gold were granted to the Marquis of Zhuxu and the Marquis of Dongmou.
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Zhuxu and the Marquis of Dongmou each received an additional two thousand households and a thousand jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 是歲，齊哀王薨，子文王則嗣。

translations.literal: That year Prince Ai of Qi died; his son Ze, Prince Wen, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: That year Prince Ai of Qi died, and his son Liu Ze, Prince Wen, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 十四年薨，無子，國除。

translations.literal: After fourteen years he died; he had no sons, and the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled fourteen years, left no heir, and the kingdom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 城陽景王章，孝文二年以朱虛侯與東牟侯興居俱立，二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Jing of Chengyang, Zhang, in the second year of Xiaowen, together with Marquis of Zhuxu and Marquis of Dongmou Xingju was established; in the second year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhang, Prince Jing of Chengyang, was enfeoffed in the second year of Emperor Wen together with his brother Xingju, Marquis of Dongmou; he died two years later.

sentences.zh: 子共王喜嗣。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Gong Xi, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Xi, Prince Gong of Chengyang, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 孝文十二年，徙王淮南，五年，復還王城陽，凡立三十三年薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Xiaowen, he was moved to be king of Huainan; in the fifth year, again returned to be king of Chengyang; in all he reigned thirty-three years and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Emperor Wen he was transferred to Huainan; five years after that he was brought back to Chengyang. He reigned thirty-three years in all before he died.

sentences.zh: 子頃王延嗣，二十六年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Qing Yan, succeeded; in twenty-six years he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Yan, Prince Qing of Chengyang, reigned twenty-six years.

sentences.zh: 子敬王義嗣，九年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Jing Yi, succeeded; in nine years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, Prince Jing, followed and reigned nine years.

sentences.zh: 子惠王武嗣，十一年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Hui Wu, succeeded; in eleven years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Wu, Prince Hui, held the throne eleven years.

sentences.zh: 子荒王順嗣，四十六年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Huang Shun, succeeded; in forty-six years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shun, Prince Huang, ruled forty-six years.

sentences.zh: 子戴王恢嗣，八年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Dai Hui, succeeded; in eight years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hui, Prince Dai, succeeded him and died after eight years.

sentences.zh: 子孝王景嗣，二十四年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Xiao Jing, succeeded; in twenty-four years he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Jing, Prince Xiao of Chengyang, reigned twenty-four years.

sentences.zh: 子哀王雲嗣，一年薨，無子，國絕。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Ai Yun, succeeded; in one year he died; he had no sons; the state was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yun, Prince Ai, lasted only a year and left no heir; the kingdom lapsed.

sentences.zh: 成帝復立雲兄俚為城陽王，王莽時絕。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng again established Yun's elder brother Li as king of Chengyang; in Wang Mang's time it was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng revived the title for Liu Li, Prince Yun's elder brother, but the line died out under Wang Mang.

sentences.zh: 濟北王興居初以東牟侯與大臣共立文帝於代邸，曰：「誅呂氏，臣無功，請與太僕滕公俱入清宮。」

translations.literal: King Xingju of Jibei, at first as Marquis of Dongmou together with the great ministers jointly established Emperor Wen at the Dai residence, saying: "In executing the Lü, your servant had no merit; I beg to enter with Grand Coachman Lord of Teng together to purge the palace."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xingju of Jibei had been Marquis of Dongmou when he helped the ministers enthrone Emperor Wen at the princely residence in Dai. "We slew the Lü," he said then, "yet I had no share in the glory. Let me join Grand Coachman Xiahou Ying in clearing the palace."

sentences.zh: 遂將少帝出，迎皇帝入宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the young emperor out and welcomed the emperor into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted the boy emperor out and brought the new sovereign in.

sentences.zh: 始誅諸呂時，朱虛侯章功尤大，大臣許盡以趙地王章，盡以梁地王興居。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when the Lü clan was being executed, Zhang, Marquis of Zhuxu, had merit above all others; the great ministers agreed to make Zhang king of all Zhao and Xingju king of all Liang.
translations.idiomatic: When the Lü clan was first being destroyed, Liu Zhang, Marquis of Zhuxu, had done the greatest service; the great ministers agreed to make Zhang king of Zhao and Xingju king of Liang.

sentences.zh: 及文帝立，聞朱虛、東牟之初欲立齊王，故黜其功。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen was established, he heard that the Marquis of Zhuxu and the Marquis of Dongmou had at first wished to set up the king of Qi, and therefore reduced their merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, he learned that the Marquis of Zhuxu and the Marquis of Dongmou had at first wished to make the king of Qi emperor, and therefore diminished their rewards.

sentences.zh: 二年，王諸子，乃割齊二郡以王章、興居。

translations.literal: In the second year, when imperial sons were enfeoffed as kings, two commanderies were cut from Qi to make Zhang and Xingju kings.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when imperial sons were invested as kings, two commanderies were carved from Qi to enfeoff Zhang and Xingju.

sentences.zh: 章、興居意自以失職奪功。

translations.literal: Zhang and Xingju inwardly thought themselves deprived of office and robbed of merit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Xingju both felt they had been stripped of deserved rank and robbed of their merit.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，章薨，而匈奴大入邊，漢多發兵，丞相灌嬰將擊之，文帝親幸太原。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year Zhang died. The Xiongnu made a major incursion on the border; the Han mobilized many troops; Chancellor Guan Ying led the attack; Emperor Wen personally visited Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: A little more than a year later Zhang died. The Xiongnu raided deeply along the frontier; the Han mobilized large forces; Chancellor Guan Ying took command; and Emperor Wen personally went to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 興居以為天子自擊胡，遂發兵反。

translations.literal: Xingju thought the Son of Heaven was personally striking the barbarians and therefore raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Xingju assumed the emperor had left the capital to fight the barbarians in person and therefore raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，罷兵歸長安，使棘蒲侯柴將軍擊破，虜濟北王。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he recalled the troops and returned to Chang'an, sent Chai the general, Marquis of Jipo, to defeat him, and captured the king of Jibei.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he recalled his forces to Chang'an and sent General Chai, Marquis of Jipo, to defeat him and capture the king of Jibei.

sentences.zh: 王自殺，國除。

translations.literal: The king killed himself; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The king killed himself, and the kingdom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 文帝憫濟北王逆亂以自滅，明年，盡封悼惠王諸子罷軍等七人為列侯。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen pitied the king of Jibei for bringing ruin on himself through rebellion; the next year he enfeoffed seven sons of Prince Daohui, including Bagun, as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying the king of Jibei for destroying himself through rebellion, the next year Emperor Wen enfeoffed seven sons of Prince Daohui, including Liu Bagun, as ranked marquises.

sentences.zh: 至十五年，齊文王又薨，無子。

translations.literal: By the fifteenth year Prince Wen of Qi again died and had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: By the fifteenth year Prince Wen of Qi had died again, leaving no heir.

sentences.zh: 時悼惠王後尚有城陽王在，文帝憐悼惠王適嗣之絕，於是乃分齊為六國，盡立前所封悼惠王子列侯見在者六人為王。

translations.literal: At that time among Prince Daohui's descendants the king of Chengyang still survived; Emperor Wen pitied the extinction of Prince Daohui's legitimate succession, and therefore divided Qi into six states and established as kings all six of Prince Daohui's sons then living who had previously been enfeoffed as ranked marquises.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Chengyang still survived among Prince Daohui's descendants; pitying the extinction of the legitimate Qi succession, Emperor Wen divided Qi into six kingdoms and invested all six of Prince Daohui's living sons who had previously held marquisates as kings.

sentences.zh: 齊孝王將閭以楊虛侯立，濟北王志以安都侯立，菑川王賢以武成侯立，膠東王雄渠以白石侯立，膠西王卬以平昌侯立，濟南王辟光以扐侯立。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Qi, Jianglü, was established from Marquis of Yangxu; Prince Zhi of Jibei from Marquis of Andu; Prince Xian of Zichuan from Marquis of Wucheng; Prince Xiongqu of Jiaodong from Marquis of Baishi; Prince Ang of Jiaoxi from Marquis of Pingchang; and Prince Piguang of Jinan from Marquis of Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jianglü became Prince Xiao of Qi from the Marquisate of Yangxu; Liu Zhi, king of Jibei, from Andu; Liu Xian of Zichuan from Wucheng; Liu Xiongqu of Jiaodong from Baishi; Liu Ang of Jiaoxi from Pingchang; and Liu Piguang of Jinan from Zhi.

sentences.zh: 孝文十六年，六王同日俱立。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Xiaowen the six kings were all established on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year of Emperor Wen all six were invested on the same day.

sentences.zh: 立十一年，孝景三年，吳楚反，膠東、膠西、菑川、濟南王皆發兵應吳楚。

translations.literal: Having been established eleven years, in the third year of Xiaojing, Wu and Chu rebelled; the kings of Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Zichuan, and Jinan all raised troops in response to Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years into his reign came the third year of Emperor Jing, when Wu and Chu rose in revolt. The kings of Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Zichuan, and Jinan all mobilized in their support.

sentences.zh: 欲與齊，齊孝王狐疑，城守不聽。

translations.literal: They wished to join with Qi; Prince Xiao of Qi hesitated, defended the city, and would not heed.
translations.idiomatic: They tried to bring Qi in, but Prince Xiao of Qi wavered, kept his walls manned, and refused their summons.

sentences.zh: 三國兵共圍齊，齊王使路中大夫告於天子。

translations.literal: The troops of the three states together besieged Qi; the king of Qi sent the road middle grandee to report to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The three rebel hosts ringed Qi, so the king dispatched his courier—the official styled "grandee in the middle of the road"—to appeal to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 天子復令路中大夫還報，告齊王堅守，漢兵今破吳楚矣。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again ordered the road middle grandee to return and report, telling the king of Qi to hold firm; Han troops had now broken Wu and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the same envoy back with orders for the king to stand fast: imperial forces had already crushed Wu and Chu.

sentences.zh: 路中大夫至，三國兵圍臨菑數重，無從入。

translations.literal: When the road middle grandee arrived, the troops of the three states besieged Linzi in many rings; there was no way to enter.
translations.idiomatic: But Linzi was wrapped in layer upon layer of siege lines, and he could not get through.

sentences.zh: 三國將與路中大夫盟曰：「若反言漢已破矣，齊趣下三國，不且見屠。」

translations.literal: The generals of the three states swore an oath with the road middle grandee, saying: "If you reverse your words that Han is already defeated, Qi will hurry to submit to the three states; if not, you will presently see slaughter."
translations.idiomatic: The rebel generals cornered him and extorted a pledge: "Tell the king the Han is finished and urge him to yield to us—or we kill you."

sentences.zh: 路中大夫既許，至城下，望見齊王，曰：「漢已發兵百萬，使太尉亞夫擊破吳楚，方引兵救齊，齊必堅守無下！」

translations.literal: The road middle grandee having promised, when he reached below the walls and saw the king of Qi, he said: "Han has already raised a million troops, sent Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu to break Wu and Chu, and is now leading troops to rescue Qi; Qi must hold firm and not submit!"
translations.idiomatic: After the Grandee of the Road had promised them, he reached the foot of the walls, caught sight of the king of Qi, and cried, "Han has already raised a million troops and sent Grand Commandant Zhou Yafu to defeat Wu and Chu. The army is now on its way to rescue Qi. Qi must hold firm and must not surrender!"

sentences.zh: 三國將誅路中大夫。

translations.literal: The generals of the three states executed the road middle grandee.
translations.idiomatic: The three generals put him to death for his treachery.

sentences.zh: 齊初圍急，陰與三國通謀，約未定，會路中大夫從漢來，其大臣乃復勸王無下三國。

translations.literal: At first, when Qi's siege was urgent, secretly it communicated with the three states in plotting; the agreement was not yet settled, when it happened that the road middle grandee came from Han; its great ministers then again urged the king not to submit to the three states.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the siege Qi had secretly dealt with the rebels, though no firm pact was sealed. When the courier returned from the capital with the emperor's message, Qi's ministers pressed the king anew to hold out against the three kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 會漢將欒布、平陽侯等兵至齊，擊破三國兵，解圍。

translations.literal: It happened that Han generals Luan Bu, Marquis of Pingyang, and others' troops reached Qi, attacked and broke the troops of the three states, and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Luan Bo and the Marquis of Pingyang arrived with other imperial columns, routed the besiegers, and raised the siege.

sentences.zh: 已後聞齊初與三國有謀，將欲移兵伐齊。

translations.literal: Afterward, hearing that at first Qi had plotted with the three states, they wished to shift troops to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the court learned of Qi's first overtures to the rebels and prepared to turn the army against Linzi.

sentences.zh: 齊孝王懼，飲藥自殺。

translations.literal: Prince Xiao of Qi feared, drank poison, and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiao of Qi, terrified at the prospect, took his own life with poison.

sentences.zh: 而膠東、膠西、濟南、菑川王皆伏誅，國除。

translations.literal: And the kings of Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Jinan, and Zichuan were all executed; their states were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The kings of Jiaodong, Jiaoxi, Jinan, and Zichuan were executed to a man and their kingdoms struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 獨濟北王在。

translations.literal: Only the king of Jibei remained.
translations.idiomatic: Only the king of Jibei survived among them.

sentences.zh: 齊孝王之自殺也，景帝聞之，以為齊首善，以迫劫有謀，非其罪也，召立孝王太子壽，是為懿王。

translations.literal: When Prince Xiao of Qi killed himself, Emperor Jing heard of it and thought that Qi had been foremost in goodness, that the coercion and plotting had not been his crime, and summoned and established Prince Xiao's heir Shou; this is Prince Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xiao of Qi killed himself, Emperor Jing judged that Qi had been foremost in loyalty, that coercion and plotting had not been his true crime, and invested Prince Xiao's heir Liu Shou as king—Prince Yi.

sentences.zh: 二十三年薨，子厲王次昌嗣。

translations.literal: After twenty-three years he died; his son Cichang, Prince Li, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled twenty-three years and died; his son Liu Cichang, Prince Li, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 其母曰紀太后。

translations.literal: His mother was called Empress Dowager Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was known as Empress Dowager Ji.

sentences.zh: 太后取其弟紀氏女為王后，王不愛。

translations.literal: The empress dowager took her younger brother Ji's clan daughter as queen for the king; the king did not love her.
translations.idiomatic: She married him to a niece of her own Ji clan, but the king cared nothing for his Ji queen.

sentences.zh: 紀太后欲其家重寵，令其長女紀翁主入王宮正其後宮無令得近王，欲令愛紀氏女。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ji wished her family to have heavy favor; she ordered her eldest daughter, Princess Ji, to enter the king's palace and regulate his rear palace, not allowing anyone to get near the king; she wished to make him love the Ji clan daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ji meant to keep power in her kin: she installed her eldest daughter, a princess by the Ji surname, inside the palace to police the harem and keep other women from the king's bed, hoping to force his affection onto the Ji girl.

sentences.zh: 王因與其姊翁主姦。

translations.literal: The king therefore committed adultery with his elder sister the princess.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the king took his sister, that same princess, as his secret lover.

sentences.zh: 齊有宦者徐甲，入事漢皇太后。

translations.literal: Qi had a eunuch Xu Jia, who entered service with the Han empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Among Qi's eunuchs was Xu Jia, who had gone to Chang'an to wait on the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 皇太后有愛女曰脩成君，脩成君非劉氏子，太后憐之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had a beloved daughter called Princess Xiucheng; Princess Xiucheng was not a child of the Liu house; the empress dowager pitied her.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager doted on a daughter named the Princess of Xiucheng—no child of the imperial Liu line—and showered her with tenderness.

sentences.zh: 脩成君有女娥，太后欲嫁之於諸侯。

translations.literal: Princess Xiucheng had a daughter E; the empress dowager wished to marry her to one of the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: The princess had a daughter, E, whom her mother hoped to marry off to a feudal king.

sentences.zh: 宦者甲乃請使齊，必令王上書請娥。

translations.literal: The eunuch Jia then requested to be sent to Qi, insisting he would make the king submit a memorial asking for E.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia volunteered for a mission to Qi, promising to bring back a formal request from the king for the girl's hand.

sentences.zh: 皇太后大喜，使甲之齊。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was greatly pleased and sent Jia to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, she dispatched him north.

sentences.zh: 時主父偃知甲之使齊以取后事，亦因謂甲：「即事成，幸言偃女願得充王後宮。」

translations.literal: At that time Zhufu Yan knew Jia was being sent to Qi to take a queen affair, and therefore also said to Jia: "If the affair succeeds, fortunately speak that Yan's daughter wishes to be able to fill the king's rear palace."
translations.idiomatic: Zhufu Yan, seeing a chance for his own daughter, pulled Xu Jia aside: "If you pull this off, put in a word for my girl as a secondary consort."

sentences.zh: 甲至齊，風以此事。

translations.literal: When Jia reached Qi, he hinted at this matter.
translations.idiomatic: In Linzi, Xu Jia sounded out the court on the match.

sentences.zh: 紀太后怒曰：「王有后，後宮備具。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Ji angrily said: "The king has a queen; the rear palace is fully provided.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ji exploded: "The king already has a queen and a full harem.

sentences.zh: 且甲，齊貧人，及為宦者入事漢，初無補益，乃欲亂吾王家！

translations.literal: Moreover Jia is a poor man of Qi who, having become a eunuch and entered service with Han, at first had no benefit, and now wishes to throw our royal house into disorder!
translations.idiomatic: As for Xu Jia—a pauper from Qi who bought his way into the Han palace—he has never done us a scrap of good, and now he would sow chaos in our house!

sentences.zh: 且主父偃何為者？

translations.literal: Moreover what is Zhufu Yan?
translations.idiomatic: And who is this Zhufu Yan?

sentences.zh: 乃欲以女充後宮！」

translations.literal: He wishes to use his daughter to fill the rear palace!"
translations.idiomatic: He thinks his daughter belongs in the inner apartments!"

sentences.zh: 甲大窮，還報皇太后曰：「王已願尚娥，然事有所害，恐如燕王。」

translations.literal: Jia was greatly cornered, returned and reported to the empress dowager, saying: "The king was already willing to marry E, yet the affair had something harmful, and he feared it would be like the king of Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jia, badly cornered, returned and reported to the empress dowager: "The king was willing to marry E, but there was danger in the matter; he feared it would be like the case of the king of Yan."

sentences.zh: 燕王者，與其子昆弟姦，坐死。

translations.literal: The king of Yan, with his son and younger brothers, committed incest and was put to death for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: He meant the scandal of the king of Yan, who had lain with his kindred and was executed for it.

sentences.zh: 故以燕感太后。

translations.literal: Therefore he used the case of Yan to move the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: He used the example of Yan to dissuade the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后曰：「毋復言嫁女齊事。」

translations.literal: The empress dowager said: "Speak no more of marrying a daughter to Qi."
translations.idiomatic: "Say no more of wedding a girl to Qi," she said.

sentences.zh: 事寖淫聞於上。

translations.literal: The affair gradually seeped and was heard by the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Whispers of the incest spread until they reached the emperor's ear.

sentences.zh: 主父偃由此與齊有隙。

translations.literal: Zhufu Yan thereby had a rift with Qi.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Zhufu Yan nursed a grudge against Qi.

sentences.zh: 偃方幸用事，因言：「齊臨菑十萬戶，巿租千金，人眾殷富，鉅於長安，非天子親弟愛子不得王此。

translations.literal: Yan was then favored and wielded power, and therefore said: "Qi's Linzi has a hundred thousand households; market rents are a thousand in gold; the people are numerous, rich, and greater than Chang'an; unless the Son of Heaven's own younger brother or beloved son, none may be king there.
translations.idiomatic: Zhufu Yan was then favored and in power, so he said, "Linzi in Qi has one hundred thousand households, and its market rents are worth a thousand in gold. Its people are numerous, prosperous, and wealthier than Chang'an. No one but the Son of Heaven's own brother or beloved son should be king there.

sentences.zh: 今齊王於親屬益疏。」

translations.literal: Now the king of Qi is ever more distant in kinship."
translations.idiomatic: Now the king of Qi is ever more distant in kinship."

sentences.zh: 乃從容言呂太后時齊欲反，及吳楚時孝王幾為亂。

translations.literal: Then at ease he spoke of how in Empress Dowager Lü's time Qi had wished to rebel, and how in the time of Wu and Chu Prince Xiao had almost made disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He reminded the throne how Qi had flirted with rebellion under Empress Lü and how Prince Xiao had nearly joined the Seven Kingdoms revolt.

sentences.zh: 今聞齊王與其姊亂。

translations.literal: Now he heard the king of Qi had committed adultery with his elder sister.
translations.idiomatic: He added the fresh rumor that the king was sleeping with his own sister.

sentences.zh: 於是武帝拜偃為齊相，且正其事。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Wu appointed Yan chancellor of Qi, and moreover to rectify the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor named Zhufu Yan chancellor of Qi with orders to get to the bottom of it.

sentences.zh: 偃至齊，急治王後宮宦者為王通於姊翁主所者，辭及王。

translations.literal: When Yan reached Qi, he urgently prosecuted the rear-palace eunuchs who for the king had communicated with the elder sister princess's place; their confessions implicated the king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhufu Yan reached Linzi and turned the screws on the harem eunuchs who had facilitated the king's visits to the princess; their testimony pointed straight at the king.

sentences.zh: 王年少，懼以罪為吏所執誅，乃飲藥自殺。

translations.literal: The king was young in years; fearing he would be seized and executed by officials for his crime, then he drank poison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Young and terrified of arrest and public execution, the king drank poison.

sentences.zh: 是時趙王懼主父偃壹出敗齊，恐其漸疏骨肉，乃上書言偃受金及輕重之短，天子亦因囚偃。

translations.literal: At this time the king of Zhao feared that Zhufu Yan in one outing had ruined Qi, and feared he would gradually estrange flesh and bone; therefore he submitted a memorial saying Yan had taken bribes and had faults of severity and lightness; the Son of Heaven therefore also imprisoned Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Zhao, alarmed that one vindictive minister could destroy a princely house and set kin against kin, memorialized that Zhufu Yan had taken bribes and committed other offenses; the emperor had him thrown in prison.

sentences.zh: 公孫弘曰：「齊王以憂死，無後，非誅偃無以塞天下之望。」

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong said: "The king of Qi died of grief, without posterity; unless Yan is executed there is no way to stop the world's expectations."
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong urged: "The king of Qi died heirless and broken-hearted; only Zhufu Yan's death will satisfy the realm."

sentences.zh: 偃遂坐誅。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon sat guilty and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhufu Yan was condemned and put to death.

sentences.zh: 濟北王

translations.literal: King of Jibei
translations.idiomatic: The king of Jibei

sentences.zh: 濟北王志，吳楚反時初亦與通謀，後堅守不發兵，故得不誅，徙王菑川。

translations.literal: King Zhi of Jibei, at the time of the Wu and Chu rebellion, at first also communicated in plotting with them; afterward he held firm and did not raise troops; therefore he was not executed, and was moved to be king of Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi of Jibei had toyed with the rebels at first but never marched; spared execution, he was transferred to the throne of Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 元朔中，齊國絕。

translations.literal: In the Yuanshuo period, the state of Qi was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanshuo the kingdom of Qi ceased to exist.

sentences.zh: 悼惠王後唯有二國：城陽、菑川。

translations.literal: After Prince Daohui there were only two states: Chengyang and Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Of Prince Daohui's line only Chengyang and Zichuan remained.

sentences.zh: 菑川地比齊，武帝為悼惠王冢園在齊，乃割臨菑東圜悼惠王冢園邑盡以予菑川，令奉祭祀。

translations.literal: Zichuan bordered Qi; Emperor Wu, because Prince Daohui's tomb park was in Qi, then cut off east of Linzi the round tomb park of Prince Daohui and its towns, entirely giving them to Zichuan, ordering it to perform the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Because Prince Daohui's mausoleum park lay east of Linzi inside old Qi territory, Emperor Wu carved that enclave out and annexed it to Zichuan so his descendant could tend the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 志立三十五年薨，是為懿王。

translations.literal: Zhi reigned thirty-five years and died; this is Prince Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhi reigned thirty-five years and is remembered posthumously as Prince Yi of Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 子靖王建嗣，二十年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Jing Jian, succeeded; in twenty years he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Jian, Prince Jing, ruled twenty years.

sentences.zh: 子頃王遺嗣，三十五年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Qing Yi, succeeded; in thirty-five years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi, Prince Qing, held the throne thirty-five years.

sentences.zh: 子思王終古嗣。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Si Zhonggu, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhonggu, Prince Si, succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 五鳳中，青州刺史奏終古使所愛奴與八子及諸御婢姦，終古或參與被席，或白晝使羸伏，犬馬交接，終古親臨觀。

translations.literal: In the Wufeng period, the Qingzhou governor memorialized that Zhonggu made his beloved male slaves fornicate with his bazhong (Eight Sons) concubines and various palace maids; Zhonggu sometimes joined them on the couch, or in broad daylight made the weak lie prone while dogs and horses copulated, Zhonggu personally watching.
translations.idiomatic: During Wufeng the governor of Qingzhou charged Liu Zhonggu with forcing his favorite male slaves on concubines of the statutory bazhong rank—the grade called 'Eight Sons'—and on other palace women, taking part himself, and—in broad daylight—making frail attendants submit to bestial coupling while he watched.

sentences.zh: 產子，輒曰：「亂不可知，使去其子。」

translations.literal: When children were born, then he said: "Disorder cannot be known; make them cast away their children."
translations.idiomatic: When children resulted, he ordered them destroyed: "We cannot tell whose seed this is—get rid of it."

sentences.zh: 事下丞相御史，奏終古位諸侯王，以令置八子，秩比六百石，所以廣嗣重祖也。

translations.literal: The affair went down to the chancellor and imperial clerk; they memorialized that Zhonggu, occupying the position of a feudal king, by ordinance had installed bazhong (Eight Sons) concubines, salary comparable to six hundred shi, by which to broaden heirs and honor the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: The case went to the chancellor and the censorate, who observed that the statutes allow a king to take bazhong concubines at six hundred bushels' stipend precisely to multiply heirs and honor his line.

sentences.zh: 而終古禽獸行，亂君臣夫婦之別，悖逆人倫，請逮捕。

translations.literal: Yet Zhonggu behaved like birds and beasts, disordering the distinction between lord and minister and husband and wife, perverse and contrary to human relations; they requested arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhonggu had conducted himself like a beast, blurring every bond of ruler and subject, husband and wife, and human decency; they demanded his arrest.

sentences.zh: 有詔削四縣。

translations.literal: There was an edict stripping four counties.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped him of four counties.

sentences.zh: 二十八年薨。

translations.literal: In twenty-eight years he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-eighth year of his reign.

sentences.zh: 子考王尚嗣，五年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Kao Shang, succeeded; in five years he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Shang, Prince Kao, reigned five years.

sentences.zh: 子孝王橫嗣，三十一年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Xiao Heng, succeeded; in thirty-one years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Heng, Prince Xiao, ruled thirty-one years.

sentences.zh: 子懷王交嗣，六年薨。

translations.literal: The son, Prince Huai Jiao, succeeded; in six years he died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jiao, Prince Huai, died after six years.

sentences.zh: 子永嗣，王莽時絕。

translations.literal: The son Yong succeeded; in Wang Mang's time it was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liu Yong inherited the title until Wang Mang extinguished the house.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：悼惠之王齊，最為大國。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: When Prince Daohui was king of Qi, it was the greatest state.
translations.idiomatic: The historian's judgment: Of all the great fiefs, Prince Daohui's Qi was the mightiest.

sentences.zh: 以海內初定，子弟少，激秦孤立亡藩輔，故大封同姓，以填天下。

translations.literal: Because within the seas had just been settled, sons and younger kin were few, stimulated by Qin's isolation and lack of screen and aid, therefore they greatly enfeoffed those of the same surname, in order to fill the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The empire was newly pacified, imperial sons were few, and the lesson of Qin's lonely fall was fresh; the court therefore lavished territory on Liu kinsmen to ring the realm with bulwarks.

sentences.zh: 時諸侯得自除御史大夫群卿以下眾官，如漢朝，漢獨為置丞相。

translations.literal: At that time the feudal lords could themselves appoint from the imperial clerk and great ministers down the multitude of officials, as in the Han court; Han alone for them established the chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Each kingdom could staff its own bureaucracy down to the clerks, mirroring the capital, save that the crown alone named each kingdom's chancellor.

sentences.zh: 自吳楚誅後，稍奪諸侯權，左官附益阿黨之法設。

translations.literal: From after Wu and Chu were executed, gradually they stripped the feudal lords' power; the laws of left-hand officials, attachment, faction, and partisan bias were established.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu and Chu were crushed, the throne steadily pared princely power—through statutes against serving princes as a "left-hand" career, against unauthorized enlargement of fiefs, and against clique loyalty.

sentences.zh: 其後諸侯唯得衣食租稅，貧者或乘牛車。

translations.literal: Thereafter the feudal lords only obtained to clothe and eat from rents and taxes; the poor among them sometimes rode ox carts.
translations.idiomatic: In time the kings kept little more than the income from their tax rolls; the poorer among them went about in ox-drawn carts.
